subject: Sunrise Retail: Vendor activation, multi-entity invoice handoff, and EU VAT reverse-charge
messages:
From: Marta Reyes <marta.reyes@sunrise-retail.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: ap-automation@sunrise-retail.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Supplier onboarding + remit entity split / VAT reverse-charge

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for confirming Redwood as a vendor for our European retail accounts. A few items to get the supplier record live in our procurement system (SupplyLink):

- Register on SupplyLink (link below) and complete the vendor profile.
- We require separate invoices per remit legal entity when a single engagement spans multiple Sunrise legal entities. Each invoice must reference the PO issued to that legal entity.
- For EU orders where reverse-charge applies, please upload your EU VAT certificate and local tax registration numbers to the portal.
- Bank details and ACH/SEPA mandate must be completed via the DocuSign link we use (see below).

Attachments: SupplyLink quickstart.pdf (instructions), sample_invoice_requirements.docx

Deadline: procurement will prioritize vendors who complete the packet within 7 business days. Once active, POs will be issued and AP will accept separate PDFs for each remit entity in a single email.

Payment terms for new vendors: standard NET 60. Procurement can discuss NET 45 with a 1% early-pay concession, subject to approval.

If you have any questions about how to present split invoices (single PDF vs multiple PDFs), cc procurement and we can confirm.

Portal: https://supplylink.sunriseretail.com/onboard?token=abc123
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345-ABCD

Regards,
Marta Reyes
Senior AP Onboarding Coordinator
Sunrise Retail AP Team
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marta Reyes <marta.reyes@sunrise-retail.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Supplier onboarding + remit entity split / VAT reverse-charge

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the clear checklist, we’ll get this started today. A few quick clarifications from our side so we set expectations with finance and legal: 

1) PO mapping: when you say "each invoice must reference the PO issued to that legal entity," can Sunrise accept a consolidated submission where each remit-entity invoice is a separate PDF file attached to one email and each PDF names the PO in the filename? Example: PO12345_Redwood-Invoice.pdf; PO67890_Redwood-Invoice.pdf.

2) EU VAT / reverse-charge evidence: we will upload our EU VAT certificate to the portal. For non-EU legal entities providing services to EU Sunrise entities, is a VAT registration or an equivalency certificate required? Please confirm exact field names in the portal (VAT number vs. tax id).

3) Payment terms: our finance team expects NET 30 by default. NET 60 will materially impact cash flow. Marcus (cc) — can you run a quick cash-impact for accepting NET 60? Also confirm if Redwood can propose the NET 45 / 1% early-pay option.

Attachments: W9_MinaHaddad.pdf (company TIN), Redwood_EU_VAT_Certificate.pdf (for portal upload).

We’ll start the SupplyLink registration now but would prefer to get confirmation on the invoice file naming and whether a single PDF containing both invoices (clearly labeled inside) is acceptable for scanning/PO matching.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Program Manager, Customer Finance
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Reyes <marta.reyes@sunrise-retail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ap-automation@sunrise-retail.com
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 08:37:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Supplier onboarding + remit entity split / VAT reverse-charge

Hi Evelyn —

Great, welcome aboard. Answers inline below: 

1) Consolidated submission: yes, procurement will accept one email with multiple attached PDFs. Each invoice must be a discrete PDF file and the filename should include the PO (recommended format: PO{number}_RemitEntityName_RedwoodInvoice.pdf). Our automated matcher relies on separate files per PO.

2) VAT fields: in SupplyLink the field is labeled "EU VAT Number". For non-EU suppliers providing services to EU Sunrise entities, we require either an EU VAT number or a documented reason (e.g., supplier is non-EU and reverse-charge applies; then attach VAT certificate or self-declaration form). If in doubt, upload your local tax ID and the EU VAT certificate — procurement will validate.

3) Payment terms: NET 60 is standard for our retail vertical. Procurement can approve NET 45 with a 1% early-pay discount; that requires an approved concession (procurement head + AP). If Redwood wants to pursue NET 45/1%, submit a short justification (expected cashflow benefit to Sunrise or strategic reasons).

I attached the SupplyLink quickstart PDF and a short AP checklist.

Attachments: SupplyLink_quickstart.pdf

Let me know when your vendor account is created and we’ll expedite PO issuance.

Best,
Marta
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Supplier onboarding + remit entity split / VAT reverse-charge — internal ask

Marcus —

Forwarding the Sunrise packet. They require separate PDFs per remit entity and NET 60 standard; procurement is open to NET 45 with a 1% early-pay concession if we provide justification. Please:

- Quick estimate of the cost to Redwood if we accept NET 45 / 1% on the expected first-year revenue from Sunrise (deal_id DL-2027-0048).
- Assess whether we can absorb 1% (or propose a partial concession) and recommend a counter-offer if needed.
- If we agree to pursue, I’ll prepare a short justification for procurement (commercial + strategic rationale).

Also: legal (Laura) — any concerns about the split remit approach (two invoices for the same engagement)? If we need a vendor master change or intercompany flow, flag the steps.

Thanks — I’ll finish the SupplyLink registration and upload the VAT certs today.

Evelyn
Senior Program Manager, Customer Finance
Redwood Inference
